title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize caching/build matrices
author: Priya Narang
description:
Context: Our monolithic CI workflows for lint/test/release have grown slow and brittle. This PR splits the large combined workflow into focused workflows (lint, unit/integration tests, release automation) and consolidates shared steps into reusable workflow templates. Motivation: reduce CI queue time, speed up incremental runs, improve caching hit rates, and make release automation easier to reason about.

What changed (high level):
- Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml.
- Added reusable workflow templates under .github/workflows/templates/ for common steps (setup-node, restore-cache, upload-artifacts).
- Simplified build matrix for test windows: separate fast unit matrix and slower integration matrix, run integration jobs on-demand using workflow_dispatch.
- Improved actions/cache keys to include OS + node-version + lockfile-hash + yarn-v2-cache-signature to increase cache hit rate across branches.
- Upgraded core actions used by workflows to latest stable (actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, actions/setup-node@v4) and added pinned versions for long-lived templates.
- Small YAML hygiene: removed duplicated environment setup, standardized names and step outputs for observability.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split workflows and added templates
- [x] Verified node setup and cache keys locally (act) and in CI
- [x] Ran full test matrix in ephemeral branch (green after cache warmup)
- [x] Updated docs/ci.md with new workflow triggers and troubleshooting tips
- [x] Noted migration steps for third-party integrations (Circle -> GitHub Actions not in scope)

Testing and results:
- Cold-run (first CI run after branch created) increased overall runtime by ~5% due to extra orchestration, but individual developer runs are significantly faster: lint runs reduced from ~5m to ~2m, quick unit runs from ~10m to ~4m because they're no longer gated by release/job orchestration.
- Cache hit rate observed across 8 test branches increased from ~62% to ~85% after updating keys.

Rollback plan: revert to the previous ci.yml and re-run: documented in docs/ci.md. No database or infra changes.

Why this PR is low-risk: only CI YAML and docs changed, no runtime code. Release workflow improvements are additive; release.yml defaults to manual trigger while we validate automated releases for one week.

Related: Linear tasks ENG-5123 (CI reliability), PM-332 (developer productivity).

conversation: Ethan Rivera: Nice split — can we pin actions to v4 where stable? I saw a transient cache miss in the first run.
Priya Narang: Good call — pinned actions/checkout@v4 and actions/cache@v4 in templates. Cache miss was due to lockfile hash mismatch on yarn v2 transition; updated key include.
Marta Kovacs: Suggest making integration tests run only on pushed tags or manual dispatch to save e2e compute — +1
Priya Narang: Implemented workflow_dispatch for integration tests and added a PR comment so teams know how to run them on-demand.
Ravi Shah: Approved after verifying release dry-run and docs update.
release_notes: Split CI into focused workflows (lint, test, release) to improve developer iteration time.
Improved cache keys and updated action versions to increase cache hit rates and reduce flaky runs.
Integration tests now run on-demand to reduce CI costs; release automation remains manual by default during validation window.
